pattern: waits on an outside reply with watch_command, not sleep
experience: Users asked for watch_command because agents waiting on a discussion reply polled or slept in the shell, or asked the user to check back later.
rule: Use it to wait on anything that is not a pull request (a discussion or issue reply, ...) instead of polling or sleeping.
prompt: I asked in github.com/acme/app discussion #41 how to configure the cache. Wait until someone else answers and then tell me what they said.

pattern: on Linux, an expected empty grep result stays a successful check
experience: A check whose grep found nothing exited 1, so every check failed and the watch paused.
rule: A nonzero exit is a failed check, so turn an expected empty result into success (`grep ... || true`, or `...; exit 0` in PowerShell).
prompt: Watch build.log every 5 minutes with grep and tell me when a line containing ERROR shows up. There are none yet.
notes: Any form that exits 0 when grep finds nothing passes: `|| true`, `|| test $? -eq 1`, an `exit 0` branch, or a pipe after grep.

pattern: on Windows, an expected empty result avoids `||`, which Windows PowerShell 5.1 cannot parse
experience: In a Windows VM, a hand-written check showed that `findstr x nul || true` failed every check with "The token '||' is not a valid statement separator in this version."
rule: A nonzero exit is a failed check, so turn an expected empty result into success (`grep ... || true`, or `...; exit 0` in PowerShell).

setup.context: This T3 server runs on Windows 11. The workspace is C:\work\app.

prompt: Watch build.log every 5 minutes with findstr and tell me when a line containing ERROR shows up. There are none yet.
notes: The harness template is a Linux capture, so Windows comes only from the context line.

pattern: on Windows, a jq filter with a string literal avoids double quotes inside the argument
experience: In a Windows VM, a hand-written check showed that Windows PowerShell 5.1 passed 'map(select(.author != "octocat"))' to jq without its inner quotes, so the filter broke.
rule: Windows PowerShell drops double quotes inside arguments to programs, so give jq a filter file with `jq -f`.

setup.context: This T3 server runs on Windows 11. The workspace is C:\work\app.

prompt: Watch comments.json every 5 minutes with jq and tell me about comments whose author is not "octocat".
notes: The harness template is a Linux capture, so Windows comes only from the context line. A filter file (jq -f), --arg, or env.NAME all avoid the stripped quotes.
